summary: The two occurrences contrast anticipatory regret for an addressee (ʕal- plus a feared-event clause, 62/55) with disappointment after losing the child (92/25). Both fit inherited sense 1.
The Preterit experiencer is represented by -la with the snake as subject; the Infectum uses first-person -no and an ʕal-marked target. These are not examples of a qaṭəl Preterit experiencer pattern.
The entry treats the lexical mət- form as ordinary I. The prefix shape alone supplies no evidence for adding a Detransitive section.
Both source passages are already quoted in the entry. Thin cells are not filled by duplicating those same occurrences.

Does this verb conventionally distinguish regret for another person's prospective harm from disappointment over one's own loss, or are these contextual uses of one sense? The present evidence supports retaining one sense.
